message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"10.26","text":"After saying these things, he ordered those possessed by demons and those gripped by diseases to be brought to him. When they had been brought, he laid his hands on them and prayed, then sent them away in good health, reminding them and the rest of the crowds to remain there in attendance for however many days he might stay there and speak. After the others had withdrawn, Peter bathed in the reservoir there together with those who wished to do so. He ordered the meal to be laid out on the ground beneath a dense canopy of trees for the sake of the shade, and had each person recline according to his rank; and so we partook of food. Then, after offering a blessing and further thanking God for the refreshment received, in accordance with the Hebrews’ customary faith, while much time still remained, he allowed us to ask about whatever we wished. And although there were twenty of us, he answered each one as each asked in turn. When evening had now come upon us, we all entered the most spacious room of the lodging together with him and slept there.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τοὺς δαιμονῶντας καὶ νόσοις ἐγκατειλημμένους","chosen":"those possessed by demons and those gripped by diseases","rationale":"The coordinated participles are rendered as two contextually natural classes. Grammatically, they could instead describe a single group suffering both conditions."},{"source_quote":"ἐνταῦθα παρεδρεύειν","chosen":"to remain there in attendance","rationale":"παρεδρεύω denotes staying close by or waiting in attendance, not merely sitting."},{"source_quote":"ὅσων ἂν ἡμερῶν ἐπιδημῶν διαλέγηται","chosen":"for however many days he might stay there and speak","rationale":"ἐπιδημέω describes remaining in a place, while διαλέγομαι may mean speak, converse, or deliver discourse."},{"source_quote":"ἐν τῷ ἐκεῖ ὑδροχοείῳ","chosen":"in the reservoir there","rationale":"ὑδροχοεῖον denotes a place where water is collected or held; “reservoir” fits the bathing context."},{"source_quote":"χαμαὶ στρωθῆναι","chosen":"the meal to be laid out on the ground","rationale":"The passive infinitive leaves what was spread unstated. The meal context supports this rendering, though couches, coverings, or a table setting are also possible."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τινὰ πυκνὴν τῶν δένδρων κόμην","chosen":"beneath a dense canopy of trees","rationale":"κόμη literally denotes hair or foliage and here forms an image of the trees’ thick leafy canopy."},{"source_quote":"κατ’ ἀξίαν ἕκαστον κατακλιθῆναι","chosen":"had each person recline according to his rank","rationale":"κατ’ ἀξίαν indicates arrangement according to worth, dignity, status, or rank."},{"source_quote":"ἐπευχαριστήσας τῷ θεῷ ἐπὶ τῷ εὐφρανθῆναι","chosen":"further thanking God for the refreshment received","rationale":"The wording denotes additional thanksgiving for being gladdened or refreshed; “for having enjoyed the meal” is another contextually possible expression."},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν Ἑβραίων συνήθη πίστιν","chosen":"in accordance with the Hebrews’ customary faith","rationale":"The rendering retains πίστις as “faith” and attaches the phrase to the blessing and thanksgiving. In this context πίστις could alternatively denote customary religious observance or practice."},{"source_quote":"ἐν μέρει ἑκάστῳ πυθομένῳ ἐπέλυσεν","chosen":"he answered each one as each asked in turn","rationale":"ἐν μέρει means “in turn,” and ἐπιλύω here means to resolve or explain what each person asked."},{"source_quote":"τὸν εὐρύτατον τῆς ξενίας οἶκον","chosen":"the most spacious room of the lodging","rationale":"οἶκος can denote a room or chamber, and ξενία here refers to the place of lodging or guest accommodation."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοὺς· ὑγιαίνοντας,","issue":"The selected edition prints a high stop between αὐτοὺς and ὑγιαίνοντας. The accusative participle naturally construes with αὐτούς, yielding “sent them away in good health.” The punctuation is editorial and does not require alteration of the Greek wording.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"χαμαὶ στρωθῆναι","issue":"The wording does not explicitly identify what was spread on the ground. The banquet context supports “the meal to be laid out,” while “couches or coverings to be spread” and “the table to be set” remain viable alternatives. This is ordinary contextual ellipsis, not evidence of omitted text.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"κατὰ τὴν Ἑβραίων συνήθη πίστιν","issue":"Both the attachment of the phrase and the contextual range of πίστις admit alternatives. It is rendered as describing the manner of the blessing and thanksgiving, with πίστις retained as “faith”; “according to the Hebrews’ customary observance/practice” is also defensible.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
